intro.label: Before They Arrive
intro.heading: What to Have Ready Before Your Miniature Poodle Puppy Comes Home
intro.html:
Miniature Poodle puppies are alert, curious, and faster to learn than most breeds you'll encounter. By the end of week one, yours will have figured out your morning routine, identified which household sounds mean something interesting is happening, and probably learned its name and sit. The intelligence is real from day one.

There are two things specific to Miniature Poodles that most general puppy checklists don't cover: the grooming habit foundation that must begin in week one (not when the adult coat arrives at 9–12 months), and the mental enrichment setup that this breed genuinely needs beyond physical exercise. This checklist covers both, along with the standard puppy setup.

care.label: The Full List
care.heading: Supplies Checklist
care.html:
Containment & Sleep

  • Small crate with divider — buy adult-sized from day one with the divider making it puppy-appropriate; a Miniature Poodle adult fits a small or medium crate
  • Soft crate liner or bed — washable; keep a spare
  • X-pen or baby gates — to contain the puppy to a supervised area during housetraining; Poodle puppies are explorers and will find their way into every accessible space

Feeding

  • Stainless steel bowls (2) — sized for a small breed puppy
  • Small-breed puppy food — continue the breeder's food initially; transition slowly to avoid stomach upset
  • Puzzle feeder or snuffle mat — feed meals through an enrichment feeder from day one; slows eating, provides mental stimulation, and establishes the habit of using their brain at mealtimes

Collar, Leash & ID

  • Small flat collar — 10–12 inches for a Miniature Poodle puppy
  • 6-foot leash — standard for training; avoid retractable leashes for puppies
  • ID tag — engraved with your phone number; have it before the puppy arrives

Grooming — Start Week One

  • Slicker brush (soft pins) — the primary at-home brushing tool for a Poodle; use from week one even though the puppy coat needs minimal work — you're building handling tolerance
  • Metal greyhound comb (medium) — follow the slicker brush with this to check for tangles; make it a habit immediately
  • Detangling spray — mist lightly before every brush session; non-negotiable for curly coat
  • Ear cleaning solution — start weekly ear cleaning from the first week; Poodles grow hair in the ear canal and ear care must become routine
  • Gentle puppy shampoo — for home baths; use a moisturizing formula suited to curly coats
  • Finger toothbrush + dog toothpaste — daily teeth brushing from week one; small breeds develop dental disease early and daily brushing is the most effective prevention
  • Nail clippers (small) — handle paws daily from the first week; actual trimming can start as soon as you're both comfortable

Enrichment & Toys — More Important for This Breed

  • Kong (small/medium) — freeze-stuffed for crate settling and mental engagement; a Poodle puppy can learn to interact with this in more complex ways as they develop
  • Puzzle feeder (Level 1) — age-appropriate at 8 weeks; upgrade difficulty as the puppy masters each level; Poodles solve beginner puzzles in days
  • Tug toy or rope toy — for interactive play; Poodles enjoy games that involve their person
  • Variety of textures — different toy types keep a smart puppy engaged; rotate rather than leaving everything out at once

Health & Safety

  • Vet appointment booked — within the first 3 days; bring PRA DNA test documentation from the breeder
  • Pet insurance applied for — before the first vet visit; epilepsy coverage is the key reason this matters for Poodles specifically
  • Enzyme cleaner — for housetraining accidents
  • Puppy-proofed space — Poodles are curious problem-solvers; they will figure out how to access things other breeds ignore; check electrical cords, cabinet latches, and small-object clearance

special.label: First Week
special.heading: The First Week Plan and Common Mistakes
special.html:
Day 1–2: Calm Entry, Early Learning

Your Poodle puppy will be alert and interested from the first hour. Keep introductions calm but don't underestimate their readiness to learn — you can start name recognition from hour one. Let them explore the designated puppy area at their own pace. The first crate night: put the crate near your bed, use a warm blanket and a ticking clock or heartbeat toy for comfort, and expect crying for 3–5 nights before it resolves. Consistency here saves weeks of difficulty later.

Day 3: First Vet Visit

Bring all health records and PRA DNA test documentation from the breeder. Ask for patella evaluation. Confirm the vaccine schedule. Ask about ear canal hair and what to watch for — your vet can show you what clean ears look like and what infection signs look like. Confirm flea/tick/heartworm prevention timing and product choice for a small breed.

Week 1: Five Daily Habits That Form the Foundation

  • Grooming handling: pin brush session daily, 5–10 minutes; also handle ears, paws, and mouth for tolerance-building
  • Teeth introduction: toothpaste on finger, gentle gum touching, building toward full brushing over the first week
  • Ear cleaning: practice applying ear solution and wiping; this habit must be established before they resist it as adults
  • Training sessions: 3–5 minutes, multiple times per day; name recognition and sit from day one; a Poodle puppy will learn both by day 3 if you're consistent
  • Puzzle feeding: feed at least one meal through a puzzle feeder or snuffle mat to start the mental stimulation habit

The Mistake Most New Poodle Owners Make

They underestimate the puppy coat transition. The soft, easy-to-manage puppy coat is replaced by the denser, curlier adult coat between 9 and 18 months. Owners who haven't established a consistent brushing routine find the transition brutal — suddenly the coat that seemed to manage itself is matting overnight. The owners whose dogs sail through this transition are invariably the ones who brushed consistently from week one, even when it seemed like the puppy coat didn't need it. Build the habit before you need it, not after.

faq.q: What food should I start my Miniature Poodle puppy on?
faq.a: Whatever the breeder has been feeding, at least for the first two weeks. After that, a small-breed puppy formula (not large-breed) with an AAFCO statement for growth. Miniature Poodles are prone to dental disease — avoid soft or wet food as the primary diet, as hard kibble provides more mechanical cleaning. If you're considering raw or home-prepared diets, discuss with your vet first; these require careful nutritional balancing.

faq.q: When should I start training a Miniature Poodle puppy?
faq.a: Day one. Poodles are the second most intelligent breed in the world by obedience and working intelligence measures, and they start learning from the moment they arrive. Name recognition, sit, and leave-it are all achievable in the first week with a Poodle puppy. Keep sessions to 3–5 minutes and several times a day — they learn fast enough that longer sessions become boredom and repetition. Enroll in puppy class after vaccines are complete; consider advanced obedience or trick training courses after that.

faq.q: Why does my Miniature Poodle puppy need puzzle feeders?
faq.a: Because the breed's intelligence requires mental stimulation as much as physical exercise. A Poodle who is physically exercised but mentally bored will invent its own entertainment — usually something you won't enjoy. Feeding meals through a puzzle feeder takes 3–5 minutes instead of 30 seconds, provides problem-solving engagement, and builds the dog's confidence and focus. It's one of the lowest-cost, highest-impact enrichment tools available. Start at the age-appropriate difficulty level and increase as they master each one.

faq.q: When can I take my Miniature Poodle puppy to the groomer?
faq.a: After the final vaccine in the series (around 16 weeks). Book an introductory appointment — a light bath, blow-dry, and table familiarization rather than a full clip. This first grooming experience sets the tone for every appointment afterward; a puppy who has a calm, positive first groomer experience is easier and less costly to groom for life. Tell your groomer it's the puppy's first appointment and ask them to prioritize a gentle, low-stress introduction over a perfect result.

faq.q: How long can a Miniature Poodle puppy be left alone?
faq.a: The same rule as all puppies: approximately one hour per month of age maximum. A 2-month-old can manage about 2 hours before bladder and anxiety limits are reached. Miniature Poodles are particularly people-oriented and don't handle extended isolation well — under-stimulated Poodles develop anxiety and stress behaviors faster than many breeds. If you work full-time, plan for a dog walker or puppy daycare before you bring the puppy home, not as an afterthought when the problem appears.
